note: THE derivation-equivalence fixture (substrate §8): a sealed (Task, Submission) pair from which two independent implementations MUST derive byte-identical tuples. It is the fixture that backs the 'derived, never authored' premise, and it carries all three of §8's named sub-cases in one document so they cannot drift apart.

cases.declaredButUnsetProfileKey: The profile declares `reviewDepth` in `requirementKeys`, but neither document sets it. It MUST be OMITTED from the tuple, never null-filled — only the four core axes are null-filled (§4.1 step 2). A deriver that null-fills every declared key produces a different digest for every task family, and the populations never join.
cases.excludedForeignKeys: `maxAttemptDurationMs` (Task side) and `network.example.customKey` (Submission side) are present in the effective requirements but are neither core axes nor profile-declared, so both are EXCLUDED. The priced consequence, stated in §4.1: two Submissions differing only on an excluded key share one tupleDigest. A family that needs an extra axis to be treatment-distinguishing must DECLARE it.
cases.enrichmentBan: `venueKnowledge` below is what a local venue actually knows at execution time — the harness binary digest. §4.1 step 3 forbids adding it: 'a venue that knows the harness binary digest does not add it to a value the requirements carried as {id, version}'. The expected canonical bytes contain no harness digest; `expect.mustNotContain` pins the exact string so a deriver that enriches fails on the substring as well as on the digest.
cases.constraintTightening: The Task constrains `model` to `{provider: anthropic}`; the Submission pins `{provider: anthropic, id: claude-haiku-4-5}`. The merge's winning value is the SUBMISSION's, byte-exactly — not the Task's constraint and not a synthesized union. §4.1 step 1: 'the winning value per key is the merge result, never either source alone'.
cases.floorTightening: The Task sets `effort: medium` (a `floor` class key declared by the profile); the Submission tightens to `high`. Same rule: the merge result, `high`, is what enters the tuple.
